newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct cash hogs seen steady - trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct cash hogs seen steady - trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady as the market revives following the Christmas holiday on Wednesday, livestock dealers said.
Activity Tuesday was extremely light amid holiday plant closures or reduced operating hours, they said.

Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota Thursday could range from $53.50 to $54.00 per cwt. Illinois top plant prices for hogs could range from $51.50 to $53.00 and Indiana/Ohio top plant prices could span $53.00 to $54.00, the dealers said.
For those plants running even reduced hours in southern Minnesota and Iowa, extremely cold temperatures and blowing snow made operations difficult at best, they said.
Below-zero temperatures and wind chills close to 50 below Fahrenheit overnight and early Tuesday severely restricted hog marketings in central and western Iowa.
Cold and blowing snow drastically reduced shipments in southern Minnesota where snowdrifts five to eight feet deep plugged rural roads, the dealers said.
"We should be running O.K by Thursday," one Minnesota hog buyer said, "I'm confident we'll get the hogs then".
